name: Vung Tau
provinceNote: The tourism catalogue and the museum still print Ba Ria–Vung Tau. The Ho May operator and Tuoi Tre’s 2026 festival report print Phường Vũng Tàu, Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh.
dotReason: Worth the night out of Ho Chi Minh City for Back Beach and the statue.
summary: A beach city on a peninsula near Ho Chi Minh City, with sandy bays and a hilltop Christ statue. Swim at Back Beach, climb to the Christ statue, ride the cable car to Ho May park, and eat banh khot, crisp mini pancakes. One or two nights suits families and weekend escapes from the city.
fee: Back Beach has no ticket on the tourism pages. Christ the King is free on the Vietnam Tourism page.
getThere: About 100 km from Ho Chi Minh City, about two hours on the tourism line. Traffic is check on arrival.
seoTitle: Vung Tau travel guide — beach, statue, and the ride
seoDescription: Back Beach is the swim, with the 32 m Christ on Small Mountain. Ho Chi Minh City is about 100 km and two hours. Mary on Big Mountain is a different figure.
intro: You wake on Back Beach to a low surf, a hotel line along the sand, and Small Mountain at the end of the bay. The other picture is the white Christ figure on that headland, arms out. Stay here if the beach and that statue are the trip. Go back to Ho Chi Minh City if you wanted the city and only borrowed a beach afternoon.

Swim on Back Beach. Vietnam Tourism describes the waves as fairly flat and suitable for children. Front Beach, the arc between the two mountains, is the evening walk and a drink after dark. The mistake is to photograph Mary, holding a child on Big Mountain, and caption her as the Christ statue. Both figures are printed at 32 metres.

Eat bánh khọt on Nguyễn Trường Tộ, one cake at a time with herbs and fish sauce. The stingray pot, crab bánh canh, and squid hủ tiếu are the other bowls Vietnam Tourism names. After the swim, the night seafood market is on the same sand: you choose the fish and the cooking. Where a price was not printed, it is Check on arrival.
gettingAround: Ho Chi Minh City is the usual previous stop. The provincial catalogue prints about 100 km by the Long Thanh–Ho Chi Minh City expressway, and about 95 km from Bien Hoa. Vietnam Tourism prints just 100 kilometres and just two hours. A minute table for traffic was not on those pages. Treat about two hours as the tourism-board figure.

Phương Trang (FUTA) and Hoa Mai are the bus companies Vietnam Tourism names. Hoa Mai luxury tickets are printed at 150,000 VND from 83 Nguyễn Thái Bình on that page. No 2026 timetable was opened, so the fare and the clock are check on arrival.

The high-speed ferry is GreenlinesDP. Saigon boarding from 28 August 2025 is Pier 4, opposite Hàm Nghi, 50 metres from the Thủ Ngư flagpole. Vietnam Tourism still sends readers to Bến Nhà Rồng and prints tickets of 120,000–250,000 VND, with a landing at Front Beach and a hydrofoil of roughly two hours. The operator’s 1 July 2026 notice prints weekday adults at 320,000 VND and weekend adults at 350,000 VND. The booking page’s child ages do not match that notice. Sailing minutes, and the Vũng Tàu pier, are check on arrival. Weather, tide, and a technical hold can cancel a boat.

On the peninsula, a motorbike taxi can reach the Christ statue. Walks the sources describe are the Back Beach sand, the seafront pavement, and the hill paths to Villa Blanche and the statue. Fares are check on arrival. Tan Son Nhat is Ho Chi Minh City’s airport. Minutes from the airport to Vung Tau are check on arrival. No rail station is named for Vung Tau.

stayAreas.name: Back Beach
stayAreas.summary: Beachfront hotels where Vietnam Tourism puts the high-end rooms, restaurants, and beach clubs. No hotel brand.

stayAreas.name: Front Beach
stayAreas.summary: The other seafront, buildings along the arc between Big Mountain and Small Mountain. The evening walk, not the main swim.

eat: Bánh khọt is the snack Vietnam Tourism says a Vung Tau trip is incomplete without. Eat it on Nguyễn Trường Tộ, one cake at a time, herbs around it, sauce on the side. The stingray pot, crab bánh canh, squid hủ tiếu, and the Back Beach night market are the other meals. Where a price was not printed, it is Check on arrival.
interestsBody: Dining starts with bánh khọt, then the stingray pot, crab bánh canh, and the seafood you choose at the Back Beach night market.
Back Beach is the morning swim. Front Beach is the arc after dark.
The white statue on Small Mountain is Christ the King. Mary on Big Mountain is a different figure.

interestGroups.title: Dining and F&B
interestGroups.summary: Bánh khọt, the stingray pot, and the night catch on Back Beach.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: The small molded cakes on Nguyễn Trường Tộ, the stingray pot, and seafood you choose on the Back Beach sand after dark.

interestGroups.title: Back Beach morning
interestGroups.summary: The swim Vietnam Tourism tells families to use, because the waves are described as flat.
body: Walk the sand at the start of the day, then swim, then an umbrella. Vietnam Tourism calls the waves fairly flat and suitable for children, and puts hotels, restaurants, and beach clubs along this strand.

Surf, stand-up paddle, and kite surf are named from the sand. Umbrella hire and water-sport hire have no printed price. Check on arrival. Vietnam Tourism prints the beach at 3 km. A single agreed length was not copied.

cards.title: Back Beach
cards.summary: Surf, wet sand, and the hotel line, with the headland at the end of the bay. The morning walk and the swim.

interestGroups.title: Front Beach after dark
interestGroups.summary: The arc between the two mountains, kept for the evening walk and a drink.
body: Front Beach is the southwest arc between Big Mountain and Small Mountain. The provincial page ties the name Tam Duong to looking for the sun, and says sunrise is the moment, while sunset is still bright on this water. Vietnam Tourism calls the evening lively and adds a drink after dark.
No bar is named. Drink prices and a closing hour are check on arrival. The 2026 whale procession left this park at 5:30. That is the festival morning, not an ordinary evening.

cards.title: Front Beach
cards.summary: The curved seafront and the water. Swim on Back Beach. Come here for sunrise, or for a drink after dark.

interestGroups.title: The white statue
interestGroups.summary: Christ the King, 32 metres, on Small Mountain above Pineapple Beach.
body: The figure people mean is Christ the King, arms out, on Small Mountain. Vietnam Tourism dates it to 1974, prints it at 32 metres, and counts about 800 steps to the feet and about 100 more to the shoulders. Entry is free on that page.

Mary on Big Mountain is also printed at 32 metres and is not this statue. The lighthouse is the early-twentieth-century tower on this same headland. Its hours and fee did not load, so it is not a separate page.

cards.title: Christ the King
cards.summary: Both arms, the head, and the climb. Free on the Vietnam Tourism page. A motorbike taxi is the alternative to the steps.

interestGroups.title: White Villa
interestGroups.summary: Bach Dinh, started in 1898, on the Front Beach side of Big Mountain.
body: Stop at the white villa on the walk toward the Big Mountain summit. Work started in 1898. The museum page prints two hour blocks and no ticket price. The building is printed at 4 Trần Phú and the relic list at 6 Trần Phú.
The French guns on the same hill are a separate relic. A licensed frame of those cannons in the open was not found, so they are not a card. Confirm the gate at the door.

cards.title: Bach Dinh
cards.summary: The white villa and the garden stair. Afternoon, on the way up the hill. The two hour lines do not match.

interestGroups.title: Big Mountain
interestGroups.summary: Mary with the child, the pagoda, and the cable car. Not the Christ statue.

blocks.heading: Mary and the pagoda
paragraphs: Our Lady of Mulberry Beach is the white Mary holding the child, on the slope above Bãi Dâu. The catalogue prints the statue built in 1992, 32 metres, at 60 metres above the sea. She is not Christ the King.

Thích Ca Phật Đài is the pagoda complex on Trần Phú: a seated figure, a 12 metre reclining figure, and the sculptures of Siddhartha’s life. The decision dates on the museum article and the catalogue do not match.

blocks.heading: The cable car
paragraphs: Ho May’s lower station is 1A Trần Phú. The scenic ticket is the round trip and the Royal Garden viewpoint, adults 100,000 VND. The full visit is adults 475,000 VND and adds the rides. Park hours are 8:00–22:00 on both operator pages. Buy the ticket that matches the visit.

cards.title: Our Lady of Mulberry Beach
cards.summary: Mary holding the child, full figure, on Big Mountain. Same printed height as Christ, different hill.

cards.title: Thich Ca Phat Dai
cards.summary: The reclining figure and the gate on Trần Phú. A separate visit from the Christ statue.

cards.title: Ho May Park
cards.summary: A cabin toward Big Mountain. Scenic adults 100,000 VND. The full visit is 475,000 VND.

interestGroups.title: The whale rite
interestGroups.summary: Fishermen greet the whale at Thắng Tam. On an ordinary day you see the hall.
body: The communal house and the whale hall worship the whale as Nam Hải. The catalogue dates the hall to the reign of Minh Mạng, 1820–1840. The relic list prints 104 Hoàng Hoa Thám.

The rite is the 16th of the 8th lunar month. In 2026 the public days were 26 and 27 September, and the boats left Front Beach at 5:30. The next solar date moves. Check on arrival. Hòn Bà, the rock at the end of Back Beach, is a low-tide crossing, not a boat you can take at any hour.

cards.title: Thang Tam whale hall
cards.summary: The whale remains in the hall on Hoàng Hoa Thám. The procession is the festival morning, not a random afternoon.

cards.title: Hon Ba
cards.summary: The shrine rock off the end of Back Beach. Cross only at low tide. Festival mornings are 5:00–9:00 in the catalogue.

faqs.q: Where should I swim in Vung Tau?
faqs.a: Back Beach. Vietnam Tourism describes the waves as fairly flat and suitable for children. Front Beach is the evening walk along the arc between the two mountains, not that swim.

season.label: Check on arrival
season.note: A dry-month or wet-month table for the peninsula was not on the Vung Tau pages used here. GreenlinesDP does not compensate when weather, tide, a natural disaster, or a technical or security hold delays or cancels a boat.
